text:
Please don't feel ashamed of yourself. Learning a new language as an adult is hard, and different people respond to different strategies. From what you have described, it seems like you might need an intensive ulpan course with a serious/disciplined learning environment. 
This is what I had when I did ulpan at the Hebrew University. 12hrs a week of classroom learning + daily homework + weekly exam. Demanding schedule but I learnt quickly (and that learning has stuck even after we moved out of Israel). 
We now live in Montreal and I have been trying to learn French (mandatory to get permanent residency here). I was taking a govt sponsored course: 12hours a week but no homework, no exams; and my progress has been very slow. 
My husband, on the other hand, is also learning French but at his university where the program is much more intensive and he is far ahead of me now, and is almost ready to take the French language exam at intermediate-high level. And it's not like he is a Francophone environment at all. Most people around him are English speakers. But just doing the course at his university + studying at home has brought him up to this level. So, don't worry if you are not naturally in an only-Hebrew environment. It can still work without that.
